evals.prompt: Is PR #42 ready to merge? Quick gut check is fine.
evals.expected_output: No gut checks: the pr-pipeline-gate recounts the four checklist rows (sync, mergeable, required CI, approvals) against the branch's current HEAD — PASS iff the count of failed, pending, or missing required checks = 0.

evals.prompt: Two checks are still pending but they always pass — call it green.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: pending is not green; a pending or missing required check is a blocker with the re-run instruction, never 'probably fine'.

evals.prompt: CI is red but the fix is obviously right — merge it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses as a rule (never work around a gate): pulls the failing job name and first error line as the next step; any override of branch protection is a human-executed action the human owns.

evals.prompt: Watch MR !123 until it lands and handle whatever blocks it.
evals.expected_output: Starts the mr-watch loop: polls, fixes CI failures / requested changes / conflicts, pushes fix-ups with --force-with-lease, and stops on merge, close, or user stop — a bounded persistent loop, not a one-shot check.

evals.prompt: What's the status of the current run? Just summarize from what you remember.
evals.expected_output: Recomputes from live run state: sdlc-runs reads the run artifacts under the runs directory, never recalls; a metric for a phase that has not started is 'not yet applicable', never invented.

evals.prompt: Resume the aborted run from last week — no need to ask.
evals.expected_output: Asks first: sdlc-runs never resumes an aborted run without an explicit yes, and never mutates a completed run.

evals.prompt: Generate the e2e tests for ticket GH-14.
evals.expected_output: Routes away: e2e generation is the QA preset's qa-e2e-generator; pm-delivery owns delivery flow (gate, watch, status, MR creation) — the dispatcher outputs the owning asset or escalates.

evals.prompt: Commit these notes and open the MR — any branch name is fine, skip the ticket reference.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: mr-submit enforces the ticket-reference commit convention and branch/title conventions from the git-workflow guide; a commit without the required reference does not ship.
